stages.legendary: Paint the same windmill one step further, between the grand and the mythic. Everything from grand stays. The base becomes dark cut stone, the top of the tower juts out on corbels like the stern castle of a galleon, with rows of small lit windows and a carved balcony in black oak and matt brass, two taut stays from the cap to iron bollards, a carved crest under the balcony, two big sacks taller than the door on an iron-bound oak carrying pole. A hint of old magic: a cool pale blue glow in the window rows. No sails, no blades and no sail frames anywhere: only the iron hub on the cap, a bare iron plate with a short axle stub, nothing attached to it. The hub stays clearly visible on the cap, big and plain. Nobody in the image, no people at all. Footprint unchanged, growth goes up and stays inside the canvas. stages.mythic: Edit the concept and go much further: much bigger, taller and far more sumptuous, as if a whole rich land had spent much more money and labour on it. Keep the same windmill: the dark slate stone base, the balustraded gallery, the tarred timber tower with its slate cap, the lookout mast with its crow's nest, the brick bakehouse and the open cart shed. Make it a great mill: a wider tower of black oak and fine cut stone with three galleries one above the other, many arched lit windows, carved stone stairs with iron rails, a second bakehouse wing and a long stone granary, iron bands, more loaded carts and stacked sacks. The towering element: from the back of the cap, behind the lookout mast and well away from the front hub, rise two curved matt ivory-coloured ribs, one taller and one chipped, standing upright side by side like the arms of a lyre, joined by five taut thick cords like a great harp, reaching far above the cap. The ribs never cross the hub and are not blades: nothing radiates from the hub, which stands alone on the front of the cap. A bright blue-white flame burns at the tip of each rib and a few pale sparks run along the cords, clear by day and by night; every window glows warm. No sails, no blades and no sail frames anywhere: only the iron hub on the cap, a bare iron plate with a short axle stub, nothing attached to it. The hub stays clearly visible on the cap, plain and big. Remove all people completely and the cloth on the shed. Nobody in the image, no people at all. Footprint unchanged, growth goes up and stays inside the canvas. No letters or runes, no hanging cloth, no hard-edged slab, no painted cast shadow, no fog patches, no sheet of grey smoke. Matte, no gloss, no gilding. Feathered natural ground patch, same iso angle, same ink outlines, warm light from the top left.
